title: Test the new zero-trust sign-in policy against five real sign-in attempts
situation: The identity team is rolling out a zero-trust sign-in policy, where every request is checked on its own merits and being on the company network earns no trust. Five recent sign-in attempts were captured for testing, including one for alice from a Tor address at 3 a.m. and one for bob from an unmanaged phone with no multi-factor authentication. We also need proof that stolen or forged access tokens are refused.
your_task: Score each sign-in request using device health, location, IP reputation, user risk, time and MFA, and record ALLOW, STEP_UP or DENY.
Issue a short-lived access token for the request that passed.
Run the step-up MFA challenge for the two borderline requests and record the final answer.
Fire five attacks at the enforcement point (replayed, wrong-scope, forged, revoked and missing tokens) and confirm each is blocked.
why_it_matters: Stolen passwords and stolen session tokens are how most account takeovers start. A policy that only checks the password once lets an attacker in for as long as the session lasts.
done_when: 1 ALLOW, 2 STEP_UP and 2 DENY decisions are recorded, each with the signals that drove it.
Carol's prod-db request is still denied after passing MFA, because her device health is too low.
Carol's source-repo request is allowed after step-up, with a 5-minute (300-second) token.
All 5 token attacks are blocked at the enforcement point.

glossary.Zero trust: A security model where no user, device or network is trusted by default, and every request is checked.
glossary.Multi-factor authentication (MFA): Proving who you are with two or more things, such as a password plus a phone prompt.
glossary.Step-up authentication: Asking for an extra proof, such as a fresh MFA prompt, when a request looks a little risky.
glossary.Policy Engine (PE): The part that decides whether a request is allowed.
glossary.Policy Administrator (PA): The part that issues, and can cancel, the access tokens the Policy Engine approves.
glossary.Policy Enforcement Point (PEP): The gate in front of the resource that checks the token on every request.
glossary.Access token: A short-lived digital pass that lets one user reach one resource.

talking_point: Tested a zero-trust conditional access policy on 5 sign-ins (1 allowed, 2 stepped up, 2 denied), showed MFA alone could not rescue an unhealthy device, and blocked all 5 token replay, forgery and scope attacks.
